title: Cotangent complex and differential basis for a polynomial algebra
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $E$ a set. Put $P=A[x_e\mid e\in E]$. For the standard cotangent complex [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] in $D(P)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the augmentation to universal differentials induces an isomorphism $L_{P/A}\simeq\Omega^1_{P/A}[0]$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. After localizing $P$, this description identifies the cotangent complex with the localized differential module in degree zero.

proof.text: Use the standard-resolution convention of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Let $Q_\bullet$ be the constant simplicial $A$-algebra on $P=A[x_e\mid e\in E]$, augmented to $P$ by the identity. Each term is a polynomial $A$-algebra and its augmentation is surjective. All faces are identities, so on the alternating-face complex the differential from degree $-n$ to degree $-n+1$ is $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i\mathrm{id}$: it is $0$ for odd $n$ and the identity for positive even $n$. Consequently $s(Q_\bullet)\to P[0]$ has identity on $H^0$ and zero negative cohomology (each negative degree belongs to a two-term identity pair). This verifies, directly, every condition for a polynomial resolution in the cited node, without assuming any finiteness of $E$.

source.place: Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), constant polynomial resolution used in Tags 08QG (lemma-pi-lower-shriek-polynomial-algebra) and 08QH (lemma-cotangent-complex-polynomial-algebra).

proof.text: Apply the comparison for polynomial resolutions in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] to $Q_\bullet\to P$. Put $M=\Omega^1_{P/A}$. The resulting differential complex is the alternating-face complex of the constant simplicial $P$-module $M$, since $\Omega^1_{Q_n/A}\otimes_{Q_n}P=M$ and all structure maps are identities. Its augmentation $a:s(M)\to M[0]$ is the identity in degree zero. More explicitly, let $j:M[0]\to s(M)$ be the identity in degree zero and let $h^{-n}:s(M)^{-n}\to s(M)^{-n-1}$ be the identity for odd $n\geq1$ and zero for even $n\geq0$. The differential formula in Step 1 gives $dh+hd=1-ja$, and $aj=1$. Thus $a$ is a homotopy equivalence. The degreewise evaluation maps from the standard resolution to the constant resolution send $\mathrm dq\otimes p$ to $p\,\mathrm d(\epsilon(q))$; composed with $a$ they are exactly the augmentation to universal differentials. The natural comparison for this morphism of polynomial resolutions therefore identifies the canonical augmentation $L_{P/A}\to M[0]$ with this isomorphism. This proves the first clause with its specified map.

The arbitrary-variable basis theorem [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] identifies $M$ with $\bigoplus_{e\in E}P\,\mathrm dx_e$, and gives $\mathrm dg=\sum_e(\partial g/\partial x_e)\,\mathrm dx_e$ with finite support. In particular the degree-zero object just obtained has precisely this differential basis. For a localization $C=T^{-1}P$, the same node gives the base-changed basis $(1\otimes\mathrm dx_e)_{e\in E}$ in $C\otimes_PM$. No finite-rank assertion is made when $E$ is infinite.

source.place: algebra.tex Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), arbitrary-variable version of its universal-derivation proof.

proof.text: Let $T\subseteq P$ be any multiplicative subset and put $C=T^{-1}P$. The ring-localization clause of [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison], applied with the bottom multiplicative subset $\{1\}\subseteq A$, gives the canonical quasi-isomorphism $L_{P/A}\otimes_PC\to L_{C/A}$. Localization is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so it preserves the augmentation quasi-isomorphism of Step 2: apply exactness to kernels and images of the differentials to identify localized cohomology with cohomology of the localized complex. Here tensor with $C$ is localization: the mutually inverse maps are $m\otimes(p/t)\mapsto pm/t$ and $m/t\mapsto m\otimes(1/t)$; the fraction equivalence and tensor balancing verify these formulas. Hence $L_{C/A}\simeq(T^{-1}M)[0]$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identifies $T^{-1}M$ with $\Omega^1_{C/A}$ by $\mathrm dp/t\mapsto t^{-1}\mathrm d(p/1)$. Both augmentations commute with this map, since on a differential generator both composites send $\mathrm dq\otimes(p/t)$ to $(p/t)\,\mathrm d(\epsilon(q)/1)$. Thus the localized description uses the canonical augmentation, and the basis of Step 3 becomes $(\mathrm d(x_e/1))_{e\in E}$. This proves the localization clause for arbitrary $T$.
